Five Concyclic Points

GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: Moving the dots keeps five marked points on one green circle, however the picture changes.
How to play: Drag any dot, or focus one and press the arrow keys. Press a button for a new or different drawing, and tick the box to show the names.
Look for the math

Drag the points and the whole drawing changes shape. Yet five marked spots keep landing on the same green circle. Which five are they, and why can they never drift apart?

The drawing

The applet starts with two lines, L1 through M and N and L2 through P and Q, meeting at X. Four circumcircles pass through M,P,X; N,P,X; M,Q,X and N,Q,X. A line through Q cuts the first two at M1,M2 and N1,N2; another line through Q cuts the last two again at M4,N4. The circle through M1,M2,N1,N2 is called (O); it cuts L1 at M3,N3. The claim is that Q, M3, N3, M4, N4 all lie on one circle.

Four points come first

The circles MPX and NPX share the points P and X, so their radical axis is the line PX, which is L2. Since Q is on L2, its powers with respect to those two circles are equal:

QM1 × QM2 = QN1 × QN2

That is exactly the condition for M1, M2, N1, N2 to sit on one circle, the dashed (O). The logic test checks it at the start, along a sweep of every handle and in 1600 other arrangements; it held every time.

Why the fifth circle agrees

Let Y be where the line QM1M2 meets L1 and Z where QN1N2 meets L1. Y has the same power with respect to (O), the circle MPX and the circle MQX, so it is their radical centre. It is also the radical centre of the circle through Q,M4,N4, the circle MPX and the circle MQX. Therefore the common chord of (O) and the circle through Q,M4,N4 passes through Y. The same argument puts Z on that chord. Both Y and Z are on L1, so L1 is the common chord: M3 and N3 are the two points where (O) meets the circle through Q,M4,N4. This is Bui Quang Tuan's proof, and it is why the five named points are concyclic. The test also checks that Y and Z have equal powers with respect to the two circles in every arrangement.

What was checked, and what was changed

The page embeds a 500 × 450 Java applet; this board uses a 500 × 420 drawing area so the old control strip does not take space. The core keeps the applet's arithmetic quirks: the radius of each circle is the mean of the three distances to the circumcenter rather than the single distance, the circle-line cut switches method at |dy| ≤ 1, and near-parallel lines give no point. The only presentation changes are the SVG layout, a Reset and a second-arrangement button, and a small margin that keeps a dragged dot inside the board. The five-point claim held at the start, at 78 single-handle positions and at every valid one of 1600 reproducible random arrangements; the largest gap from the common circle was below a millionth of a board unit.

Press Other arrangement, then drag Q. The green circle moves with it, but it still gathers Q, M3, N3, M4 and N4.
